_comment: Precision-gate baseline (breakwater-quality-policy.md), widened corpus. Real open-source corpus, not synthetic. Regenerate with tools/CorpusScan/run-scan.ps1 and diff against this file before every release (a rise in findings-per-1000-operations needs a reviewed reason, per the quality policy's noise-regression clause). Supersedes the M10 baseline (4 repos, 65 files, 45 findings, findingsPer1000Operations 25.2) -- that data is kept below in "priorBaseline" for the diff trail, not deleted, since the rise this session is explained (see findingsPer1000OperationsNote), not a regression.
milestone: Robustness-Testing agent, widened corpus (parallel session alongside CodeFixes and PR-comment-action work)

sources.name: bitwarden-postgres
sources.note: 162 candidate files, 7 excluded (using Bit.Core/Bit.EfShared -- a cross-project dependency this tool does not check out, see toolFixesThisSession). New this session: real production Postgres migrations, large/long-running project (2021-2026 history).

sources.note: 140 candidate files, 5 excluded, same reason. New this session.

approxOperationCountMethod: grep count of migrationBuilder.<Method>( call sites across all copied corpus files -- a proxy for MigrationContext.OperationCount, not the exact analyzer-internal figure, same methodology as the M10 baseline
findingsPer1000OperationsNote: Up from 25.2 (M10, 45/1786). Reviewed reason, not a regression: the new sources are real production data-migration-heavy codebases (bitwarden's Postgres/MySQL/Sqlite migrations average far more AlterColumn/UpdateData/schema-and-data-in-one-migration operations per file than eShop/abp/eShopOnWeb's simpler CRUD-shaped migrations -- see BW013's 44 findings, a rule that fired 0 times in the M10 corpus and only exists to catch exactly this shape). Per-source finding rates vary widely (eShop 11/9 files vs bitwarden-mysql 215/155 files) confirming this is corpus composition, not a rule getting noisier: no rule's own precision (legitimate/reviewed) dropped -- see byRule below, still 100% legitimate on every sampled rule.

byRule.note: Zero findings in M10; fired for the first time this session (bitwarden's RenameColumn calls).

Sample capped at 50 per the precision gate (>50 findings). Spot-checked including a full-file read of bitwarden-mysql's UpdateNullConstraints.cs (UpdateData nulls-to-empty-string immediately followed by AlterColumn to NOT NULL on the same column) -- a textbook-correct real data-prep-then-constraint pattern, confirming the rule reads the actual EF-supplied old/new nullability correctly at scale.
Zero findings in M10; fired for the first time this session.

Sample capped at 50. Every sampled finding is a plain CreateIndex on a pre-existing table with no provider-concurrent annotation -- structurally sound given the rule only fires on the operation shape itself.
Zero findings in M10; fired for the first time this session (bitwarden's Grant table PK rebuild).

Zero findings in M10; fired for the first time this session. Includes a genuine unconditional UPDATE (no WHERE clause, confirmed by reading the full statement) and a DROP PROCEDURE IF EXISTS. See the BW035+ candidates note in breakwater-memory.md on the DROP-then-CREATE-same-name idiom this rule cannot distinguish from a destructive drop -- flagged as a precision nuance, not a bug (the policy's own principle: DROP always flags, by design).

Zero findings in M10 (this rule's trigger shape -- a data operation sharing a transaction with a schema operation in the same Up -- did not occur in the smaller/simpler corpus at all). Every finding this session is a real UpdateData immediately preceding an AlterColumn on the same column (bitwarden's null-backfill-then-NOT-NULL pattern), confirming the rule's design intent against real code for the first time.

Sample capped at 50. Spot-verified the M10 same-migration-table fix (MigrationAnalyzer.BuildContext) still holds at this scale: checked one sampled finding ('BlgUsers' risky-operation count) against grep for BlgUsers' own CreateTable and confirmed it lives in a different, earlier migration file -- the exemption correctly does not apply across migrations, only within one Up method.

Zero findings in M10 (the M10 corpus had essentially no real MySQL-provider migrations to exercise this rule against). All 28 findings are in bitwarden-mysql, all structurally correct: N operations in one Up, no wrapping transaction, MySQL provider detected -- MySQL genuinely does not support transactional DDL, so every one of these is a real risk, not a heuristic guess.

noSeverityChangesThisSession: No rule's tier was changed. Every rule that fired stayed at 100% reviewed-legitimate, matching or exceeding its shipped tier's bar. The prior session's BW022 fix (same-migration-table exemption) was spot-re-verified, not re-fixed -- no new analyzer defect was found this session.

rulesWithZeroCorpusFindings.changedFromM10: BW003, BW006, BW009, BW010, BW013, BW029 moved out of this list this session (previously zero-finding, now have real corpus findings, see byRule above) -- direct evidence that a wider/more varied corpus gives previously-silent rules a real chance to fire, as M10's own 'what's still owed' note anticipated.
rulesWithZeroCorpusFindings.policy: Rules that fire on nothing in the corpus are checked with hand-written cases instead and ship as Warning only if the pattern is unambiguous (breakwater-quality-policy.md).
rulesWithZeroCorpusFindings.verdict: Same judgment call as M10: the existing tests/Breakwater.Analyzers.Tests/*RuleTests.cs suite plus each rule's compiling docs/rules/BW0xx.md example (verified by DocumentationTests.cs) are the hand-written cases the policy calls for. Not re-verified line-by-line this session (out of scope for a corpus-widening task); still true as of the 255-test green run this session confirmed.
rulesWithZeroCorpusFindings.corpusSizeCaveat: 516 real migration files across 9 repos (up from 65/4) is materially larger and more varied (adds Postgres/MySQL/Sqlite production migrations at scale, not just SQL-Server-flavored/generic ones), but provider-specific rules needing an explicit non-default breakwater_provider/breakwater_deploy_model config (BW014's Postgres-only enum-type-change check, BW020's Postgres lock_timeout, strict-only rules generally) still were not exercised with that config turned on in this scan -- the scan runs with breakwater_profile=strict to surface strict-tier rules' raw counts, but does not set breakwater_provider explicitly, relying on the same auto-detection heuristic real users get by default. Widening sources.json further (more MySQL-heavy repos, explicit provider-override scan runs) remains a further-improvement item, not required for this session's task.

toolFixesThisSession: run-scan.ps1's default -OutDir parameter ("$PSScriptRoot/results") evaluated to an empty string under Windows PowerShell 5.1 when left at its default (a default parameter value referencing $PSScriptRoot is bound before the script body runs, when $PSScriptRoot is not yet populated in this PS version) -- results silently landed at the filesystem root (D:\results) instead of tools/CorpusScan/results. Fixed: -OutDir now defaults to unset and is resolved to "$PSScriptRoot/results" in the script body, after $PSScriptRoot is valid.

A handful of migration files in bitwarden's Postgres/MySql/Sqlite sources reference a sibling project's namespace via `using Bit.Core...`/`using Bit.EfShared...` (helper base classes/extensions outside the Migrations folder this tool checks out) -- a CS0234 namespace-not-found *error*, which (unlike a resolvable-type CS0246 already in the NoWarn list) is not suppressible and silently blocked the whole source's analyzer SARIF output, producing 0 findings for otherwise-healthy 150+ file sources. Fixed: these few files (7/7/5 across the three bitwarden sources) are now excluded up front and counted/logged separately, not silently dropped.

platformplatform's migration files carry a [DbContext(typeof(SomeDbContext))] class attribute; the DbContext type lives outside the checked-out Migrations folder, a real CS0246 that (being an error, not a warning) NoWarn cannot suppress and which blocked all analyzer output for that source. Fixed: the attribute is stripped from the copied file (irrelevant to every rule -- only [Migration("id")], handled separately for BW028, matters).

platformplatform's migration files omit `using System;`, relying on a repo-wide GlobalUsings.cs this tool does not check out, causing CS0246 on bare BCL types like DateTimeOffset. Fixed: the throwaway csproj now sets <ImplicitUsings>enable</ImplicitUsings>.

None of these were analyzer/rule bugs -- all four are scan-tool robustness fixes in tools/CorpusScan/run-scan.ps1, following the same precedent as M10's Designer.cs-attribute and SARIF-semicolon fixes.
